title: The scalar-valued tensor-test functor on an algebraic space
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $Y$ be an $S$-scheme with a specified isomorphism $e:Y\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Use the unbounded module derived category on the equivalent small ringed model and its full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, with the normalized derived tensor product, from [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. For any $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, define the tensor-test functor
$$T_E:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow D(A),\qquad K\longmapsto R\Gamma_{X,A}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}E).$$
Here $R\Gamma_{X,A}$ is the canonical $A$-valued right derived sections functor with the action induced by $X\to Y\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sfb-space-affine-global-sections]. On a morphism $a:K\to L$, the functor applies derived sections to $a\otimes^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{id}_E$. This definition is valid for every $E$; for perfect $E$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] it is the perfect tensor test used in Stacks Tag 0CX6. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or preservation-of-products assertion is part of this definition.
